outcome: As of 13 October 2026 I found no event that settles this problem, and none that claims to: the Ultimate-L conjecture (Woodin's canonical inner model containing the large cardinals) is still described as open in every opened source from 2024 to 2026. The post-2024 items bearing on it are conditional (a conditional refutation via exacting cardinals whose consistency is unestablished, a conditional HOD absoluteness constraint, a conditional analysis of the conjecture's consequences), or are unrefereed Zenodo postings by one author identity: one (31 Dec 2025) claims a canonical inner model L[E] for a single supercompact cardinal and an equiconsistency of PFA with a supercompact; one (4 Feb 2026) analyses the conjecture's consequences and lists 'the resolution of the Continuum Hypothesis' among them.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone: (a) that there is an 'ultimate core model', i.e. a single model of the kind called a core model; (b) that it is a core model (the statement uses the term 'core model' and links to the article 'Core model', so the requirement is that it be a core model in the core-model-program sense, which I infer rather than read off the bullet); (c) that it contains all large cardinals, where the bullet does not say which large cardinal notions count as 'all' or whether the model must contain them or merely be compatible with them (the Wikipedia link is 'Large cardinal property', which does not settle this); (d) that it be found, i.e. exhibited or identified and not only shown to exist (the verb is 'finding'). The bullet names no parameters: no supercompact or extendible cardinal, no HOD, no canonicity criterion. Parts (a) to (d) are one question, listed separately so that events can be placed against each.

events.what_happened: In a Quanta Magazine article (Wolchover, 26 Nov 2013) Woodin is reported to have completed the first of a four-stage proof of the Ultimate-L conjecture, to be checking the work privately with a small group of colleagues, and to be 'very optimistic about stage two', hoping to finish the proof the following summer. He says that if the conjecture is proven 'one proves the existence of ultimate L'. No written argument is cited in the article.
events.delivers: Nothing is delivered in the article: it reports a claimed partial proof (stage one of four) that is not written up in the article and not verified there. If the claim were realised it would be a proof of the Ultimate-L conjecture in full generality, but the article gives no statement of what the stages are.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. Stages two to four are not reported as complete in any source I found; the 2017 Midrasha lectures (event woodin-2017-in-search-of-ultimate-L) still describe the solution as requiring a fundamental change to inner model theory.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 years 10 months; I found no later report that stages two to four were completed
events.doubts: Only stage one is claimed, and that claim rests on a press interview; the article says the work was being checked privately and names no checker. I found no later statement from Woodin or anyone else that the four-stage proof was completed or abandoned.
events.direction: Toward the positive side: the conjecture (existence of Ultimate L, with the continuum hypothesis true in it) is the claimed target. Claimed progress only.

events.what_happened: W. Hugh Woodin, 'In Search of Ultimate-L: The 19th Midrasha Mathematicae Lectures', Bulletin of Symbolic Logic 23(1) (2017), pp. 1–109, DOI 10.1017/bsl.2016.34, published online 3 April 2017. The abstract says the solution to the inner model problem for one supercompact cardinal would yield an ultimate version of L, and that current inner model theory must be fundamentally altered to reach that solution. The reference list cites 'The axiom V = Ultimate-L' (2016), 'The Ultimate-L Conjecture' (2016, 419 pp.) and 'Fine structure at the finite levels of supercompactness' (2016, 710 pp.) as works in preparation. Date given is the journal year; the earliest written argument is not established by the sources I read, and the cited 2016 manuscripts are not found in any source I opened.
events.delivers: Exposition and programme: it states the Ultimate-L conjecture as the target and argues that the inner model programme must be altered to reach a supercompact-level canonical model. It establishes no instance and no proof of the conjecture.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (Association for Symbolic Logic)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for set theory expository work
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the lectures; refereeing is implied by publication but I did not verify it

events.time_since_posted: about 9 years (journal date); the cited 2016 manuscripts are not located
events.doubts: The abstract makes no claim to prove the conjecture; the cited 'Ultimate-L Conjecture' manuscript (2016, 419 pp.) is not found in any source I opened and its status is unknown.
events.direction: None on the conjecture: an exposition that frames the problem and argues that the standard inner model approaches must change.

events.what_happened: Rupert McCallum, 'New Large Cardinal Axioms and the Ultimate-L Program', arXiv:1812.03837 (math.LO), first posted 10 Dec 2018. Introduces α-tremendous, hyper-tremendous, α-enormous, hyper-enormous and virtually ω-enormous cardinals; the abstract says a proper class of α-enormous cardinals (for every limit α>0) can be shown to imply a version of the Ultimate-L conjecture. It also states an unconditional result: an elementary embedding j: V_{λ+2} → V_{λ+2} is inconsistent with ZF.
events.revisions: v2 18 Dec 2018; v3 26 Dec 2018; v4 9 Mar 2019; v5 14 Oct 2020; v6 20 Oct 2020; v7 9 Mar 2021 (current, as listed on the abstract page)
events.delivers: A conditional implication: a proper class of α-enormous cardinals implies 'a version of the Ultimate-L Conjecture'. Which version, and whether it yields the full conjecture as stated in problem_asks, is not visible in the abstract. The inconsistency result about j: V_{λ+2} → V_{λ+2} is a theorem about ZF and is not about the problem.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: the implication is from a large cardinal hypothesis whose consistency the abstract does not address, and the conclusion is a version of the conjecture, not the conjecture.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 years 10 months; no later engagement found
events.doubts: The consistency of a proper class of α-enormous cardinals is not addressed in the abstract I read; the full text was not opened.
events.direction: Conditional, toward the positive side: large cardinal hypotheses of this kind would imply a version of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Joan Bagaria, Peter Koellner, W. Hugh Woodin, 'Large Cardinals Beyond Choice', Bulletin of Symbolic Logic 25(3) (2019), pp. 283–318, DOI 10.1017/bsl.2019.28, published online 20 Aug 2019. Contrasts the 'close' and 'far' outcomes of Woodin's HOD dichotomy; the inner model side is where Woodin's Ultimate-L conjecture would support 'close'; the authors develop a hierarchy of choiceless large cardinals (starting from Reinhardt cardinals) on the 'far' side. The abstract states: 'if these choiceless large cardinals are consistent then the Ultimate-L Conjecture must fail.'
events.delivers: A conditional refutation route: consistency of the choiceless large cardinal hierarchy (not established by the paper) would refute the conjecture. Establishes no refutation.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks; the conditional's hypothesis is open.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (Association for Symbolic Logic)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article; refereeing implied, not verified

events.doubts: The consistency of the choiceless hierarchy is the open hypothesis; the paper's stake is conditional. I read only the abstract summary.
events.direction: Conditional, against the conjecture: if the choiceless large cardinals are consistent, the conjecture fails.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'Some combinatorial properties of Ultimate L and V', arXiv:2007.04812 (math.LO), posted 9 Jul 2020, one version, 33 pages. Results include: a regular cardinal above the first strongly compact carrying an indecomposable ultrafilter is measurable; any successor almost strongly compact of uncountable cofinality is strongly compact; no nontrivial cardinal-preserving embedding from V into an inner model if there is a proper class of strongly compacts; and, if κ is strongly compact, V is a set-forcing extension of κ-HOD. The abstract says the constraints coincide with those of the Ultrapower Axiom, which is expected to hold in Ultimate L, and offers this as evidence for the Ultimate-L conjecture.
events.delivers: Evidence for the conjecture: its constraints match those of the Ultrapower Axiom. The listed results are theorems about strongly compact cardinals and HOD, not about a canonical core model containing all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Evidence only; the abstract makes no claim to prove the conjecture. The full text was not opened.
events.direction: Evidence toward the positive side, not a result on existence.

events.what_happened: Joan Bagaria, Claudio Ternullo, 'Steel's Programme: Evidential Framework, the Core and Ultimate-L', arXiv:2011.14724 (math.LO, math.HO), v1 30 Nov 2020, v2 2 Aug 2021. Evaluates whether the core of Steel's multiverse could be Ultimate-L and whether a Core Universist could justify V = Ultimate-L as the best extension of ZFC. The search results give a Review of Symbolic Logic (2023) publication; I did not verify that in an opened source.
events.delivers: No mathematical result. A philosophical assessment of the hypothesis that the core is Ultimate-L. It states the hypothesis as under discussion, not established.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 years 10 months (for the arXiv posting)
events.doubts: None of substance for this problem; it is a methodological paper. Its publication status rests on a search snippet.
events.direction: None on existence; discusses the hypothesis that the core is Ultimate-L.

events.what_happened: Farmer Schlutzenberg, 'Varsovian models ω', arXiv:2212.14878 (math.LO), v1 30 Dec 2022, v2 13 May 2025 (corrected acknowledgements, updated references). Works with the minimal iterable proper class mouse N_ω (a limit of Woodin cardinals that is also a limit of strong cardinals). The abstract claims that under an unproven assumption about *-translation, the core model K for N_ω is an iterate of N_ω, is an inner model of V_ω, and is fully iterable. The abstract says the write-up of the P-constructions 'is yet to be completed'.
events.delivers: A core model K below a mouse with ω Woodin cardinals, conditional on an unproven assumption. This is a core model below a bounded large cardinal level, not a core model containing all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, including the question of an ultimate core model; the abstract does not mention Ultimate-L.
events.doubts: The main results are conditional on an unproven assumption, and the abstract says the write-up is unfinished.
events.direction: Does not bear on existence of a model with all large cardinals: it constructs a core model for a specific mouse under a condition.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, Jonathan Osiński, Alejandro Poveda, 'On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy', arXiv:2411.03558 (math.LO), posted 5 Nov 2024, one version. Consistency results about Woodin's HOD hypothesis near extendibility: the first extendible can be the first strongly compact in HOD; under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible is C(1)-supercompact in HOD; the HOD hypothesis is consistent with a club of HOD-regular cardinals below δ with κ^+HOD < κ^+.
events.delivers: Consistency results about HOD near extendible and supercompact cardinals. The abstract does not name Ultimate-L or the HOD conjecture as a statement about the existence of a core model with all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. This is HOD structure, which the Ultimate-L conjecture predicts (HOD close to V), not a construction of a model.
events.doubts: None specific to this problem. The main theorem on 'optimality' is not in the abstract I read.
events.direction: None on the problem: consistency results about HOD under the HOD hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Alejandro Poveda, 'Axiom A and supercompactness', arXiv:2406.12776 (math.LO), submitted 18 June 2024, one version. Constructs a model in which every supercompact cardinal is C(1)-supercompact with inaccessible targets, from a new axiom A compatible with Woodin's I0 cardinals. Ultimate-L appears only in the body: Theorem 3.8 is explicitly conditional on Woodin's conjecture that V = Ultimate-L implies EEA, and §1 says 'if Woodin's prospects are true, our Main Theorem provides a fairly exotic model for supercompactness'. The abstract does not mention Ultimate-L.
events.delivers: A model of supercompactness with axiom A, conditionally related to V = Ultimate-L through EEA. It delivers no statement about the existence of a canonical model containing all large cardinals; the Ultimate-L relation is a conditional, not a proof.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Conditional on Woodin's conjecture by the author's own words. I read §1 to §4 of the HTML; §5 and later were not read.
events.direction: Does not bear on existence; the Ultimate-L link is conditional and runs through an open implication (V = Ultimate-L implies EEA).

events.what_happened: Juan P. Aguilera, Joan Bagaria, Philipp Lücke, 'Large cardinals, structural reflection, and the HOD Conjecture', arXiv:2411.11568 (math.LO), v1 18 Nov 2024. Introduces exacting cardinals and ultraexacting cardinals. The abstract states: an exacting cardinal implies V ≠ HOD; an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal implies the 'V is far from HOD' alternative of Woodin's HOD Dichotomy; the consistency of ZFC with an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal 'would refute Woodin's HOD Conjecture and Ultimate-L Conjecture'; ultraexacting cardinals are consistent with ZFC relative to an I0 embedding.
events.revisions: v2 28 Aug 2025; v3 3 Sep 2025; v4 16 Sep 2025 (current, per the abstract page)
events.delivers: A conditional refutation of the Ultimate-L conjecture: if ZFC plus an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal is consistent, the conjecture fails. The paper does not prove that consistency. Its ultraexacting result is a consistency result relative to I0, not about the problem.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, unless the consistency hypothesis is established. The hypothesis's consistency strength is open; a later search summary reports it lies between I3 and I2 (see ABGG 2025 and LP 2026).
events.time_since_posted: about 23 months; four revisions in 2025 and no published version or review found
events.doubts: The refutation is conditional on a consistency hypothesis not established. The overlapping paper ABGG 2025 (event aguilera-bagaria-goldberg-lucke-2025-beyond-HOD) states that an extendible cardinal above an exacting cardinal does not refute the HOD Hypothesis; the two papers use hypotheses in opposite orders and I did not reconcile them (I read abstracts only). No independent review or publication found.
events.direction: Conditional, against the conjecture: consistency of an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal would refute the Ultimate-L conjecture.

events.what_happened: Sandra Müller, Grigor Sargsyan, 'Gödel's Program in Set Theory', arXiv:2412.07325 (math.LO), v1 10 Dec 2024, v2 12 Dec 2024. Expository survey. The abstract presents V = Ultimate-L as 'a compelling candidate for an axiom that could solve Gödel's problem' and describes the Sealing scenario. In §5 they state that CH holds if V = Ultimate-L (because CH and ¬CH are Σ2-expressible and CH holds in HOD of L(A,R) for universally Baire A), and the Conclusion asks 'Does Woodin's axiom V = Ultimate-L hold?' as an open question. Published in Monatshefte für Mathematik (special volume in honour of Gödel), 2025, DOI 10.1007/s00605-025-02086-x.
events.revisions: v2 12 Dec 2024; journal version Monatshefte für Mathematik 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s00605-025-02086-x)
events.delivers: No new result on the problem. It states the candidate axiom and its consequence CH conditionally on the axiom, and records the question as open.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.

checked_by.who: Monatshefte für Mathematik (Springer), special volume in honour of Gödel
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the volume; the authors are set theorists (Müller and Sargsyan) but they are the authors, not independent checkers
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the survey in the special volume; refereeing implied, not verified

events.doubts: None on a result; the survey itself flags the axiom's status as open.
events.direction: None: expository, and the survey treats V = Ultimate-L as a candidate, with its CH consequence conditional on it.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Siskind, 'The uniqueness of the core model', arXiv:2501.14076 (math.LO), submitted 23 Jan 2025, one version. Shows that in some contexts abstract properties uniquely determine the Jensen–Steel core model K, whose definition depends on a choice of premouse hierarchy.
events.delivers: Uniqueness of the Jensen–Steel core model K in some contexts. K is a core model below the level of one Woodin cardinal (existence follows from the absence of an inner model with a Woodin cardinal); it is not an ultimate core model containing all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. The result concerns the existing core model K, not a model containing all large cardinals.
events.doubts: None for this problem. Scope is clearly different: uniqueness of K, not an ultimate model. Abstract only read.
events.direction: None on the problem; it is a core model result, a different object from the one the problem asks for.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, Dan Hathaway, 'On (Σ²₁)^uB Absoluteness Between V and HOD', arXiv:2505.01393 (math.LO), v1 2 May 2025, v2 8 May 2025. Combines Woodin's Σ²₁ basis theorem for AD+ with Vopěnka's theorem: if there is a proper class of Woodin cardinals, every (Σ²₁)^uB statement true in V is true in HOD (also with a real parameter whose complement has OD universally Baire scales). The abstract adds that the stronger (∀R)(Σ²₁)^uB absoluteness between HOD and V 'cannot be implied by any large cardinal axiom consistent with the axiom V = Ultimate L'.
events.delivers: Absoluteness between V and HOD for (Σ²₁)^uB statements under a proper class of Woodin cardinals, and a constraint: the stronger absoluteness cannot be derived from large cardinals consistent with V = Ultimate L. Neither gives a model.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. The constraint bears on the Ultimate-L axiom's relation to large cardinals, not on the existence or construction of a canonical model containing all large cardinals.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months; preprint, no journal publication found
events.doubts: Preprint only; abstract read, full text not opened.
events.direction: Constraint on Ultimate L: it cuts against large-cardinal derivation of the stronger absoluteness, and does not decide the existence question.

events.what_happened: Juan P. Aguilera, Joan Bagaria, Gabriel Goldberg, Philipp Lücke, 'Large cardinals beyond HOD', arXiv:2509.10254 (math.LO), submitted 12 Sep 2025, one version listed. Abstract, as read: ultraexacting cardinals are equiconsistent with I0; exacting cardinals have consistency strength strictly between I3 and I2; I2 implies the consistency of Vopěnka's Principle with an exacting cardinal and the HOD Hypothesis; 'the existence of an extendible cardinal above an exacting cardinal does not refute the HOD Hypothesis'. Ultimate-L is not mentioned in the abstract.
events.delivers: Consistency-strength bounds for exacting and ultraexacting cardinals, and a claim that an extendible above an exacting does not refute the HOD Hypothesis. It does not address the Ultimate-L conjecture directly.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Its claim about extendible above exacting is in the opposite order from event aguilera-bagaria-lucke-2024-exacting-cardinals and bears on the same hypotheses. I did not reconcile the two. Abstract only.
events.direction: None on the conjecture directly; bears on the consistency strength of the hypothesis used in the 2024 conditional refutation.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 18109660, 'Inner Model Theory for Supercompact Cardinals and the Consistency of the Proper Forcing Axiom', creators listed as 'Revista, Zen' and 'MFC, 10' (both linked to ORCID 0009-0007-6299-2008; affiliation 'Revista Científica'); published 31 Dec 2025, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18109660, CC BY 4.0, file revistazen.pdf (250.8 kB). The abstract, as reported by my fetch tool (not verbatim), claims to: construct a canonical inner model L[E] for a supercompact cardinal, extending the hyper-Woodin hierarchy with an extender sequence allowing long extenders; give a comparison process for mice exhibiting λ-supercompactness, said to resolve an iterability problem for extenders overlapping Woodin cardinals; show that a supercompact in the core model K yields a forcing extension satisfying PFA and PFA yields an inner model with a supercompact; and conclude an equiconsistency of ZFC plus a supercompact with ZFC plus PFA. The page's subject label reads 'Mathematical Applications of Science Fiction' (as reported by my fetch). The copyright line names Paulo Sérgio de Andrade, who is not listed as a creator.
events.delivers: As claimed: a canonical inner model L[E] for one supercompact cardinal (not, per the abstract, a model containing all large cardinals), plus a PFA equiconsistency. The page itself verifies none of this. The PDF was not readable through my tools.
events.remains: Per the claims as summarised: whether L[E] contains all large cardinals (not claimed); whether it is a core model in the sense of problem_asks (a canonical model for one supercompact is not stated to be); the Ultimate-L conjecture as stated; and whether the claimed PFA equiconsistency and comparison result hold.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 months; I found no review, citation or engagement
events.doubts: (1) Venue: a Zenodo deposit; the page names no journal, no peer review and no affiliation beyond 'Revista Científica'. (2) Authorship: creator names 'Revista, Zen' and 'MFC, 10' are unusual; I found no set-theory record under these names. A Zenodo record of a Paulo Sérgio de Andrade (different ORCID prefix, 0009-0004) concerns topological invariants and complexity. (3) Internal tension: the same author identity's record of 7 Jan 2026 (event zenodo-2026-01-07-PFA-monograph) describes 'recent work by Viale and Weiss suggesting a possible equiconsistency' of PFA with a supercompact, while this record claims the equiconsistency as established. (4) Claimed comparison result resolving an iterability problem: unverified. (5) The subject label 'Mathematical Applications of Science Fiction' (as reported by my fetch). None of these is a verdict; the later pass weighs them.
events.direction: Claims a positive partial object (canonical model for one supercompact) and a PFA equiconsistency. Its bearing on the problem depends on whether the object contains all large cardinals, which it does not claim.
events.object: Claimed: a canonical inner model L[E] for a supercompact cardinal, built from a fully iterable extender sequence E allowing long extenders, extending the hyper-Woodin hierarchy. The construction is described only in the abstract; the PDF was not readable. Not stated to be explicit or non-constructive.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 18167647, 'Woodin Cardinals and the Consistency Strength of the Proper Forcing Axiom relative to Supercompactness', same creator identity and ORCID as the 31 Dec 2025 record, published 7 Jan 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18167647, CC BY 4.0, resource type 'Journal article', described as a monograph. The abstract covers the consistency of PFA from a supercompact, lower bounds (including inner models with Woodin cardinals derived from PFA), and Steel's theorem that PFA implies AD in L(R). It describes 'recent work by Viale and Weiss suggesting a possible equiconsistency' with a supercompact cardinal.
events.delivers: A survey of PFA consistency strength; the abstract does not claim new theorems. It does not bear on a canonical core model containing all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Relevant chiefly as a cross-check on the 31 Dec 2025 record: this record treats the PFA equiconsistency as a possibility suggested by others, while the earlier record claims it. The record does not say whether it presents new theorems.
events.direction: None on the problem.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 18485224, 'The Ultimate L Conjecture and Inner Models for Supercompact Cardinals', creators 'Revista, Zen' and 'MFC, 10' (same ORCID), affiliation 'Revista Científica', published 4 Feb 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18485224, CC BY 4.0, resource type 'Journal article' (no journal named), file PSA.pdf (242.8 kB). The description, as reported by my fetch (paraphrase, not verbatim): studies the Ultimate-L conjecture (a weak extender model for a supercompact cardinal satisfying V = Ultimate-L), analyses its consequences including the HOD Dichotomy, a Universality Theorem for weak extender models, and 'the resolution of the Continuum Hypothesis', and argues that inner model theory must move from pure extender models to strategic extender models to reach supercompactness.
events.delivers: As stated: analysis of consequences of the conjecture, which the abstract frames as conditional on it. Whether the CH resolution is conditional is not clear from the abstract as reported. No object is exhibited.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks; the paper's own framing (consequences of the conjecture) does not settle existence.
events.doubts: Venue and authorship as for the 31 Dec 2025 record. Its CH consequence, if it is unconditional, would be a claim that no one has checked; if it is conditional, it adds nothing beyond Müller–Sargsyan §5. The PDF was not readable through my tools, so I could not confirm which.
events.direction: Conditional analysis toward the positive side; the CH consequence is claimed, its status unclear.

events.what_happened: Douglas Blue, Paul Larson, Grigor Sargsyan, 'The failure of square at all uncountable cardinals is weaker than a Woodin limit of Woodin cardinals', arXiv:2602.13077 (math.LO), submitted 13 Feb 2026, one version. Forces AC over the least initial segment of a Nairian model of ZF; square fails at every uncountable cardinal and every regular cardinal is ω-strongly measurable in HOD; concludes the HOD Hypothesis is not provable in ZFC.
events.delivers: Failure of square everywhere within the reach of inner model theory, and non-provability of the HOD Hypothesis in ZFC. Neither is an ultimate core model.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: None for this problem. A search snippet described its introduction as bearing on PFA equiconsistency; the abstract page I opened does not show this, so I do not rely on it.
events.direction: None on the problem.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, Grigor Sargsyan, Benjamin Siskind, 'Ultrapowers of determinacy models as iteration trees on HOD', arXiv:2603.20951 (math.LO), submitted 21 Mar 2026, one version. Answers a question of Woodin's positively: the ultrapower of HOD by any ultrafilter on an ordinal is given by an iteration tree on HOD according to its fine-structural extender sequence and canonical iteration strategy.
events.delivers: A structural result on HOD ultrapowers. Its abstract does not mention Ultimate-L or the HOD conjecture.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: None for this problem. Abstract only.
events.direction: None on the problem.

events.what_happened: Philipp Lücke, Alejandro Poveda, 'The effects of forcing on exacting and ultraexacting cardinals', arXiv:2609.32338 (math.LO), submitted 26 Sep 2026, one version. From an I2-embedding, a set-sized transitive model of ZFC with a proper class of exacting cardinals (via Magidor support products of Prikry forcings); under Woodin's HOD Conjecture, no exacting cardinal is a limit of exacting cardinals; a Levy–Solovay analogue under the HOD Conjecture; a ZFC forcing extension with a regular cardinal that is a stationary limit of ultraexacting cardinals. Ultimate-L is not mentioned on the abstract page.
events.delivers: Consistency of exacting cardinals relative to an I2-embedding, and conditional structural results. This bears on the consistency hypothesis of event aguilera-bagaria-lucke-2024-exacting-cardinals (relative consistency with I2 is not the same as consistency of exacting above extendible in ZFC). It does not give a model containing all large cardinals.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks; the refutation hypothesis of the 2024 paper is not shown consistent by this paper.
events.doubts: Abstract only. Its consistency results are relative to I2 and do not include an extendible cardinal above an exacting cardinal, as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: None on existence; relevant to the strength of the hypothesis behind the conditional refutation.

disputes.summary: The 2024 paper aguilera-bagaria-lucke-2024 (arXiv 2411.11568 v4) says the consistency of ZFC with an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal would refute the HOD Conjecture and the Ultimate-L conjecture. The 2025 paper aguilera-bagaria-goldberg-lucke-2025 (arXiv 2509.10254) says an extendible cardinal above an exacting cardinal does not refute the HOD Hypothesis. The two concern the same hypotheses in opposite orders; I read abstracts only and did not reconcile them.

A 2024 paper by Goldberg, Osiński and Poveda is reported in a search snippet to say that a 2023 paper by Goldberg claimed Woodin proved that under the HOD hypothesis every extendible cardinal is extendible in HOD, and that Woodin never claimed this; the authors say the error was Goldberg's alone. This snippet is not from an opened page; the arXiv abstract page for 2411.03558 that I opened does not show it. It concerns HOD structure, not the Ultimate-L conjecture directly.

summary: I searched for the problem under its name, under 'ultimate L', 'Ultimate-L', 'core model' and 'HOD' vocabulary, for 2024–2026 developments, and for AI involvement, and opened the sources listed. The problem is Wikipedia's bullet 'The problem of finding the ultimate core model, one that contains all large cardinals', in the Set theory section, linked to 'Core model' and 'Large cardinal property'. The literature identifies the central formal target as Woodin's Ultimate-L conjecture (for an extendible or supercompact δ, a weak extender model N ⊆ HOD satisfying V = Ultimate-L). I recorded the statement as written, and noted that the bullet itself does not name a supercompact, HOD or a canonicity criterion. On the sources I could open, the conjecture is open as of 13 October 2026. Woodin's own 2017 exposition says current inner model theory must be fundamentally altered to reach it; the 2013 press report of a four-stage proof, stage one complete, has no later written completion I could find; Müller and Sargsyan (Dec 2024, published 2025) state it as a candidate and its CH consequence as conditional on it. The 2024–2026 papers give conditional results only. The conditional refutation of Aguilera, Bagaria and Lücke (2024, revised 2025) rests on the consistency of an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal, which is not established; its companion ABGG (2025) and Lücke–Poveda (2026) give related consistency-strength results that I did not reconcile. Goldberg (2020) and McCallum (2018) give evidence and conditional implications respectively. The two Zenodo postings by one author identity are the closest claims to the problem's object: the 31 Dec 2025 record claims a canonical inner model L[E] for one supercompact (not stated to contain all large cardinals) and an equiconsistency of PFA with a supercompact; the 4 Feb 2026 record lists a resolution of CH among consequences of the conjecture. Neither is refereed, neither names a journal, and I could not read their PDFs. The same identity's Jan 2026 record calls the PFA equiconsistency a possibility, which is in tension with the Dec 2025 claim. I rate neither as a settlement: the later pass should weigh them as unverified postings. On AI: no event on this problem credits any AI system; I found no set-theory manuscript in OpenAI's 6 October 2026 release (722 manuscripts, 372 families) in the catalogue text I could read, and the ten 'Astra' results named in a secondary article are not set theory. A 2026 IAS talk on 'Can AI Discover Truth Which is Beyond Proof?' with Woodin as speaker is a discussion, not a claimed result. Close calls: the 2013 press claim (claimed partial proof, not written) and the Zenodo claims (claimed object, unverified) are the two items a later pass could read as progress; I recorded both and did not classify them. The 2024 exacting-cardinal refutation is conditional and I recorded it as such. Several events were read from abstracts only, so their 'delivers' are as strong as the abstract, not the paper.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record as progress: the Zenodo 31 Dec 2025 posting claims a canonical inner model L[E] for a supercompact with an equiconsistency of PFA, which if correct would be a construction of a canonical model at the level the problem names and a new consistency result. Against it: no refereeing, no journal, no named expert engagement, an internal tension with the same author's Jan 2026 record, and the containment of only one supercompact rather than all large cardinals. The strongest case for reading the 2024 exacting-cardinal paper as a refutation: it states an unconditional-looking conclusion ('would refute'). Against it: the hypothesis is conditional on a consistency not established, and the companion 2025 paper uses the hypotheses in the opposite order with a non-refutation conclusion.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A refereed paper or a released manuscript proving the Ultimate-L conjecture or constructing a canonical model containing the large cardinals in the problem's sense: Woodin's 2016 'The Ultimate-L Conjecture' manuscript (419 pp., cited as in preparation in 2017), if it is released, or a refereed version of the 2013 four-stage programme. (2) Expert verification or refutation of the 31 Dec 2025 and 4 Feb 2026 Zenodo claims, from set theorists who can name the flaw or confirm the construction, and an explanation of the authorship identity. (3) A proof that ZFC plus an exacting cardinal above an extendible cardinal is consistent, or a refutation of that consistency, which would decide the 2024 conditional. (4) A reconciliation of the two Aguilera–Bagaria et al. papers on the hypothesis order. (5) The full text of arXiv 2406.12776 §5 and of the Zenodo PDFs, to see whether any claim goes beyond its abstract.

events.credibility_reason: A press-interview claim of stage one of four, with no written argument and no later report that the proof was completed.

Several F10 signals together: it claims to solve the long-open inner model problem for a supercompact, a landmark, yet has had no uptake in about 9 months; the authorship is opaque ('Revista, Zen', 'MFC, 10') with no record in set theory; the venue reviews nothing and carries the subject label 'Mathematical Applications of Science Fiction'; the same author identity's Jan 2026 record calls the claimed PFA equiconsistency only a possibility; and later expert work still treats the supercompact-level model as open.
Unrefereed Zenodo deposit under an opaque author identity. It is a survey and claims no new result.

Same opaque author identity and same non-reviewing venue as the Dec 2025 record. It lists a 'resolution of the Continuum Hypothesis' with no uptake, while expert surveys still treat V = Ultimate-L, and CH under it, as open.

judgement.why: The statement asks for a core model that contains all large cardinals. No event exhibits one, proves that one exists, or refutes its existence. The expert papers are expositions, conditional implications, or results on HOD and exacting cardinals that do not move the question, so they score none. The conditional refutation via exacting cardinals is none, because its hypothesis is not established. Schlutzenberg's paper and Siskind's are about core models at bounded large-cardinal levels, a changed question, so they are variant. The close call was the Dec 2025 Zenodo claim of a canonical model for one supercompact. Even taken at face value, it does not contain all large cardinals, so it is variant rather than case. It is also not_credible: opaque authorship, a non-reviewing venue with an odd subject label, an internal contradiction with the same identity's Jan 2026 record, and no uptake on a claim that would be a landmark. No AI was involved in any event.
judgement.doubts: Most events were read from abstracts only. The Zenodo claims are paraphrased by a fetch tool, and their PDFs were not read. The 2017 and 2019 dates are journal years, but both fall well before the snapshot. Calling the journal-published expositions 'digested' does not matter here, because they score none.
